page: Microsoft Azure E64as_v7 is an Easv7-family virtual machine configured with 64 vCPUs and 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server features 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor with dedicated CPU allocation. There is no bundled local storage, though the instance is Premium Storage capable, and it does not include any GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in several key areas. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng and Passmark CPU scores both rank in the top 10%, supported by top-tier single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression speeds. Multi-core performance and memory bandwidth, both cached and uncached, fall into the top 25%. Database operations and small-to-medium LLM inference tasks also demonstrate top-tier execution speeds, while large-model LLM inference processes at average speeds.

Given its memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8, this server offers a resource-dense profile suitable for memory-intensive workloads without the added cost of bundled local storage or GPU hardware. It is highly suited for database operations, memory-cached web serving, data compression tasks, and medium-scale language model inference.
